intro_line: A chaotic, charming riverside capital waking to a new airport.
note: Typical figures for planning; check hours and prices on the day.

climate.source: Open-Meteo historical weather, 2015-2024 averages (rain days = days with 1 mm or more)

months.note: January: dry and mild, highs near 31°C. The best month for walking the sights.
February: the driest month, only about 2 rain days. Hot at 33°C by afternoon; start early.
March: hotter at 34°C and still mostly dry. Carry water and plan shade breaks.
April: the hottest month, 35°C highs, with rain days jumping to about 14. Do sights before 10am.
May: the wet season starts, about 25 rain days. Expect heavy afternoon downpours and high humidity.
June: wet and warm, around 24 rain days. Short showers, then sun; keep plans flexible.
July: similar to June, about 24 rain days and 32°C highs. Rivers run high.
August: the wettest stretch, about 26 rain days. Pack a light rain jacket.
September: peak rain, about 28 rain days. Flooded streets are possible; allow extra travel time.
October: still wet, about 25 rain days, but rain eases late in the month.
November: rain drops to about 16 days and highs stay near 31°C. A good shoulder month.
December: dry and cooler, about 7 rain days. Comfortable days and the busiest tourist season.

killing-field.best: Morning; pair with Tuol Sleng on the same day

national-museum.best: Midday, when it is hottest outside

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Royal Palace, the genocide memorials and a food-and-riverside evening; add a night for a slower pace in the heat.

airports.name: Techo International Airport
airports.note: New main airport since 9 Sep 2025; about 20 km from the centre, so allow extra time.

options.to: Kouch Kanong Roundabout via AEON Mall 3
options.note: Runs 05:30-23:30 every 10 min; pay exact, no change given.
App price is fixed; drivers may need help with pickup points.
Agree the fare first; show clean, untorn dollar notes before paying.
Cheaper but slow and exposed to traffic fumes.

transit.best: Ride apps (PassApp, Grab, TADA) for fixed prices; city buses if you are on a tight budget.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Do not plan around rail in the city.
13 city bus lines run about 05:30–20:30. Fare is 1,500 riel; drivers give no change, so pay exact.
PassApp, Grab and TADA show fixed prices, so no haggling. Tuk-tuks cost about US$2–3 in town and US$8 to the airport; agree the fare first if you hail one.
The easy way around town: about US$2–3 a ride. Always agree the fare before you get in.
Not recommended for visitors. Motorbikes rent for US$5–6 a day, but traffic is chaotic and theft is common; park in guarded areas.
Fine for short blocks near the riverside and palace, but heat and traffic make longer walks unpleasant. Bicycles and cyclos are slow but scenic; bike hire is US$1–3 a day.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year, with a dry season roughly November to April and a wet season May to October.

items.title: Best time: November to February
items.text: Highs 31–33°C and few rain days. The most comfortable months for walking and temples.

items.title: Hottest in March and April
items.text: Highs reach 34–35°C. Sightsee before 10am and rest in air-conditioning at midday.

items.title: Wet season May to October
items.text: Rain on 24–28 days a month, usually as heavy afternoon showers. Mornings are often clear.

items.title: Humid year-round
items.text: Lows stay 23–26°C, so nights are warm and sticky. Light, breathable clothes help.

items.title: Flooding in the peak rains
items.text: September and October can flood streets. Wear sandals and allow extra time for tuk-tuks.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, a hat, sunscreen and insect repellent; a rain jacket or umbrella for May to October; modest dress for temples.
